paragraphs.en: KEYWORDS : World Action Model, Autonomous Driving, Embodied Control
paragraphs.zh: 关键词：世界动作模型、自动驾驶、具身控制

paragraphs.en: Physical intelligence [ 1 , 2 ] , including autonomous driving [ 3 ] and embodied control [ 4 ] , holds the promise of freeing human workers from physical tasks that are dangerous, laborious, or tedious. A general-purpose physical agent should not only act from visual observations, but also anticipate the physical consequences of their actions. Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, including those standard models [ 5 , 6 , 7 ] and specialized end-to-end ones [ 8 , 9 , 10 ] , typically predict actions directly without explicitly modeling the future evolution of the environment. This has motivated a shift toward World Action Models (WAMs) [ 4 , 11 , 12 , 13 ] for physical AI, which build on pretrained video generative models [ 14 , 15 ] to jointly predict future visual states and their corresponding actions.
paragraphs.zh: 物理智能 [ 1 , 2 ]，包括自动驾驶 [ 3 ] 和具身控制 [ 4 ]，有望将人类劳动者从危险、费力或繁琐的体力任务中解放出来。 一个通用的物理智能体不仅应能基于视觉观察进行行动，还应能预见其行动的物理后果。 现有的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型，包括标准模型 [ 5 , 6 , 7 ] 和专用的端到端模型 [ 8 , 9 , 10 ]，通常直接预测动作，而没有对环境的未来演化进行显式建模。 这推动了面向物理人工智能的世界动作模型（WAM）[ 4 , 11 , 12 , 13 ] 的发展，这类模型在预训练视频生成模型 [ 14 , 15 ] 的基础上，联合预测未来的视觉状态及其对应的动作。

paragraphs.en: However, WAMs follow the imagine-then-execute paradigm [ 16 , 12 ] and incur prohibitive inference latency, rendering them impractical for latency-critical applications such as autonomous driving. Borrowing few-step techniques from image and video generation, some methods apply step distillation [ 17 ] to reduce this latency, but often at the expense of a substantial drop in control accuracy, as illustrated in Fig. 1 . To address this issue, efforts [ 4 , 11 ] propose to switch from the imagine-then-execute paradigm to direct-policy WAMs. These methods retain video prediction as a training-time objective that shapes physically grounded representations, without synthesizing future observations at test time. This direct-policy formulation is more than 3 × 3\times faster than the imagine-then-execute paradigm.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，世界自回归模型（WAM）遵循“先想象后执行”范式 [16, 12]，并带来极高的推理延迟，使其在自动驾驶等对延迟敏感的应用中难以实用。 一些方法借鉴图像与视频生成领域的少步技术，采用步数蒸馏 [17] 来降低该延迟，但往往会以控制精度的显著下降为代价，如图 1 所示。 为解决这一问题，相关工作 [4, 11] 提出从“先想象后执行”范式转向直接策略式世界自回归模型。 这些方法将视频预测保留为训练阶段的目标，用于塑造具有物理基础的表征，而在测试阶段不再合成未来的观测。 这种直接策略式的构建方式比“先想象后执行”范式快 3 × 3\times 倍以上。

paragraphs.en: Despite this speedup, efficiently generating high-quality actions remains a key challenge for direct-policy WAMs. They require tens of denoising steps to achieve competitive action quality, resulting in latency that remains too high for real-time applications such as autonomous driving. This bottleneck cannot be resolved by reducing the number of denoising steps. Specifically, as shown in Fig. 2 , the performance degrades as the step count decreases, dropping by 20 % 20\% on NAVSIM (autonomous driving) and 40 % 40\% on RoboTwin (embodied control) in the one-step setting. We attribute this to the lack of action structure in random noise: multiple denoising steps can gradually impose temporal and physical consistency, whereas one-step generation must recover a coherent action sequence in a single update. Existing few-step accelerations, such as step distillation [ 17 ] and trajectory rectification [ 18 ] , still start from Gaussian noise and, therefore, do not supply the missing action prior. This motivates introducing structured action priors at initialization, providing an informed starting point for high-quality action generation in a single denoising step.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管有这种加速，高效生成高质量动作仍然是直接策略世界动作模型（WAM）面临的关键挑战。 它们需要数十个去噪步骤才能达到有竞争力的动作质量，导致延迟对于自动驾驶等实时应用而言仍然过高。 这一瓶颈无法通过减少去噪步骤的数量来解决。 具体而言，如图2所示，性能随着步数的减少而下降，在一步设置下，NAVSIM（自动驾驶）上下降20%20\%，RoboTwin（具身控制）上下降40%40\%。 我们将其归因于随机噪声中缺乏动作结构：多个去噪步骤可以逐步施加时序和物理一致性，而一步生成必须在单次更新中恢复连贯的动作序列。 现有的少步加速方法，如步数蒸馏[17]和轨迹校正[18]，仍然从高斯噪声出发，因此无法提供缺失的动作先验。 这促使我们在初始化时引入结构化动作先验，为单步去噪生成高质量动作提供一个有依据的起点。

paragraphs.en: In addition, direct-policy WAMs [ 4 , 11 ] remain limited in their ability to exploit future dynamics for effective control. They use a consistent first-frame-only interface during training and inference, relying on video co-training to encode future dynamics into the current representation. However, compressing all future information into a single first-frame representation may provide insufficient temporal context for effective future-aware control. To address this limitation, subsequent methods reintroduce future features at inference and mitigate the associated rollout cost through caching, sparse interaction [ 19 ] , or compact latent representations [ 20 ] . Despite these efforts to reduce rollout cost, generating and incorporating future features at test time still incurs additional inference overhead.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，直接策略型 WAM [4, 11] 在利用未来动态以实现有效控制方面的能力仍然有限。 它们在训练和推理阶段均采用仅使用首帧的一致性接口，依靠视频协同训练将未来动态编码到当前表示中。 然而，将所有未来信息压缩到单一的首帧表示中，可能无法提供足够的时间上下文来实现有效的未来感知控制。 为解决这一局限，后续方法在推理阶段重新引入未来特征，并通过缓存、稀疏交互 [19] 或紧凑的潜在表示 [20] 来降低相应的滚动成本。 尽管在降低滚动成本方面做了这些努力，在测试时生成并融合未来特征仍会带来额外的推理开销。

paragraphs.en: To address the aforementioned issues, we propose OSWAM , a world action model with one-step action generation for more effective physical control. Our key observation is that previous one-step action generation methods fail mainly because the action diffusion processing is initialized from unstructured Gaussian noise. To supply the missing action structure, we learn a compact set of imagination tokens from the video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) and use them as structured start points for action denoising. These tokens are far fewer than video first-frame tokens and are obtained in a single forward pass, so they add negligible computation, yet they interact with visual features to accumulate physically grounded, action-relevant context. We then noise the imagination tokens to an intermediate timestep and decode them with the action DiT in one step, replacing the long denoising trajectory required by random initialization. To enhance future-aware control, we train these imagination tokens with privileged-information distillation. A teacher attends to visual tokens over the full future horizon, while the student imagination tokens, at test time, attend only to the first frame. By distilling the teacher’s privileged representations into the imagination tokens and subsequently into the action DiT, OSWAM transfers long-horizon context without reintroducing future-dependent features at inference. This design preserves the first-frame-only interface of direct-policy WAMs, while enabling high-quality action generation in a single denoising step.
paragraphs.zh: 为解决上述问题，我们提出 OSWAM，一种具有一步动作生成的世界动作模型，以实现更有效的物理控制。 我们的关键观察是，以往的一步动作生成方法之所以失败，主要原因是动作扩散过程从非结构化的高斯噪声初始化。 为了补充缺失的动作结构，我们从视频 Diffusion Transformer（DiT）中学习一组紧凑的想象词元（imagination tokens），并将其作为动作去噪的结构化起始点。 这些词元远少于视频首帧词元，且只需一次前向传播即可获得，因此带来的计算开销可以忽略不计，但它们能与视觉特征交互，积累有物理依据的、与动作相关的上下文。 然后我们将想象词元加噪到某个中间时间步，并用动作 DiT 一步解码，从而取代随机初始化所需的长去噪轨迹。 为了增强具有前瞻性的控制，我们通过特权信息蒸馏来训练这些想象词元。 教师可以关注完整未来时间范围内的视觉词元，而学生想象词元在测试时只能关注首帧。 通过将教师的特权表示蒸馏到想象词元中，再进而蒸馏到动作 DiT 中，OSWAM 在推理时无需重新引入依赖未来的特征，即可传递长时程上下文。 这种设计保留了直接策略型世界动作模型仅使用首帧的接口，同时能在单个去噪步骤中生成高质量的动作。

paragraphs.en: Autonomous driving has recently shifted from modular pipelines with separate perception [ 21 , 22 , 23 , 24 ] and planning [ 25 ] modules toward end-to-end frameworks [ 26 ] . To further integrate future dynamics modeling, world models [ 14 , 27 , 28 , 29 ] for autonomous driving have recently been extended into world action models (WAMs). Existing methods fall into two categories: bird’s-eye view (BEV)-based and video-generation-based world models. BEV-based approaches [ 10 , 30 , 31 ] forecast occupancy evolution and ego motion, predict future latent scene features, or infer future BEV layouts for online trajectory evaluation. They are computationally efficient but do not exploit large-scale video generative priors. A complementary line of research leverages pretrained video generators and predicts the future in the image domain. These methods [ 32 , 13 , 33 ] transfer such priors to driving, but jointly rolling out video features at test time remains inefficient. SimWAM [ 11 ] follows the direct-policy design of Fast-WAM [ 4 ] to avoid test-time video rollout, yet the remaining multi-step denoising is still impractical for onboard driving. In contrast, our proposed OSWAM inherits large-scale video generative priors without test-time video rollout, and reduces action generation to a single denoising step.

paragraphs.en: Unlike autonomous driving, where compact BEV representations naturally encode road topology and traffic interactions, embodied control needs to model fine-grained object interactions and appearance changes in close-range scenes. As these phenomena are naturally captured in video, embodied WAMs are predominantly built on pretrained video generators for image-domain future modeling in two ways: explicit future imagination and direct-policy inference. Explicit-imagination methods [ 12 , 16 ] generate future visual representations at test time to guide action prediction, incurring substantial rollout latency. Direct-policy WAMs [ 4 ] retain video prediction as a training signal but generate actions directly from current observations, avoiding test-time visual rollout; however, its iterative action denoising remains a bottleneck for high-frequency closed-loop control. In contrast, OSWAM preserves large-scale video-generative priors without test-time visual rollout and reduces action generation to a single denoising step.

paragraphs.en: The main deployment bottleneck for WAMs lies in the high computational cost of diffusion-based video and action generators, whose test-time latency is prohibitive for onboard driving and closed-loop manipulation. Drawing one-step distillation from video generation, Flash-WAM [ 17 ] compresses joint video-action diffusion to a single denoising step per modality, but still synthesizes future video at inference. Fast-WAM [ 4 ] removes test-time video rollout by predicting actions from current observations only, yet retains iterative action denoising. Light-WAM [ 34 ] further replaces the generative action expert with a lightweight fusion head for single-pass action prediction, but underperforms on challenging benchmarks such as RoboTwin. SimWAM [ 11 ] follows Fast-WAM to drop test-time video rollout, but its multi-step action denoising keeps inference latency well above the budget required for onboard deployment. Building on this video-rollout-free direct-policy formulation, OSWAM addresses the remaining action-generation bottleneck through one-step action denoising.

paragraphs.en: An overview of OSWAM is shown in Fig. 3 . As in previous works [ 4 , 11 ] , we consider predicting an action chunk 𝐚 1 : H \mathbf{a}_{1:H} from the current frame f 0 f_{0} and an optional task instruction l l , with ego-state information additionally provided for driving tasks. We follow Fast-WAM in the world model backbone configuration and direct-policy setting. Specifically, the Video DiT uses the Wan2.2-5B backbone [ 14 ] , accompanied by its pretrained T5 text encoder and video VAE. The Action DiT is initialized by interpolating and downsampling the pretrained Video DiT weights. For autonomous driving, we add an ego encoder to encode the ego state and the driving command. The task languages and ego states are both provided to all tokens through cross-attention. The full model is organized as a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture with shared attention between the video and action blocks. paragraphs.en: Unlike prior direct-policy methods, which use the Video DiT at inference solely to encode the first-frame visual feature for Action DiT through shared MoT attention, OSWAM additionally introduces two groups of imagination tokens into the Video DiT: Action Imagination Tokens (AIT) and Scene Imagination Tokens (SIT). As shown in Fig. 3 , both AIT and SIT are initialized from noise in the Video DiT and interact with the first-frame visual features. The resulting AIT representation then replaces the unstructured Gaussian initialization of the Action DiT, providing a compact, structured start point for action denoising. SIT provides additional latent slots that aggregate scene context for AIT; they are updated indirectly through privileged distillation and the auxiliary action loss on AIT. Together, AIT and SIT comprise far fewer tokens than the first-frame visual input and therefore introduce only a small computational overhead during inference. To strengthen future-aware control under this first-frame-only interface, we introduce privileged-information distillation. The privileged teacher comprises a Video DiT with AIT that attends to visual tokens over the full clip, while the AIT in OSWAM attends only first-frame visual context. By aligning OSWAM’s intermediate imagination token features with those of the teacher, we transfer this privileged information to improve action generation, while OSWAM remains first-frame-only at inference.

paragraphs.en: During distillation, we freeze the teacher and provide it with ground-truth video latents over the full future horizon. The first-frame latents remain clean, while all future-frame latents are corrupted with noise at a fixed diffusion timestep τ v T \tau_{v}^{T} before the teacher forward pass. The teacher’s AIT remains initialized from pure noise at t max t_{\max} and acquires privileged information by attending to these future video tokens. OSWAM retains its standard training procedure, using a randomly sampled video timestep and the fixed AIT timestep t max t_{\max} . The teacher and OSWAM share the same video noise and action noise samples, respectively. We then align OSWAM’s AIT features with the corresponding teacher features at a set of Video DiT blocks 𝒥 \mathcal{J} , providing multi-depth distillation supervision. SIT is supervised indirectly through their attention connections to AIT. At inference, the teacher is discarded, preserving OSWAM’s first-frame-only interface without additional computation.

paragraphs.en: Autonomous Driving. For autonomous driving, we evaluate OSWAM on the NAVSIM [ 43 ] , which provides real-world driving data sampled at 2Hz, with eight cameras covering a 360-degree field of view and LiDAR observations. The dataset comprises 1192 scenarios for training and 136 scenarios for testing. NAVSIM introduces practical and reliable metrics that effectively bridge open-loop and closed-loop evaluation. Specifically, NAVSIM evaluates model performance using the Predictive Driver Model Score (PDMS), which is calculated based on five factors: No At-Fault Collision (NC), Drivable Area Compliance (DAC), Time-to-Collision (TTC), Comfort (Comf.), and Ego Progress (EP). We report PDMS, which is calculated as PDMS = NC × DAC × ( 5 × EP + 5 × TTC + 2 × C ) / 12 . \mathrm{PDMS}=\mathrm{NC}\times\mathrm{DAC}\times({5\times\mathrm{EP}+5\times\mathrm{TTC}+2\times\mathrm{C}})/{12}.
paragraphs.zh: 自动驾驶。 对于自动驾驶，我们在 NAVSIM [43] 上评估 OSWAM，该基准提供以 2Hz 采样的真实世界驾驶数据，包括覆盖 360 度视野的八个相机以及激光雷达观测。 该数据集包含 1192 个用于训练的场景和 136 个用于测试的场景。 NAVSIM 引入了实用且可靠的指标，有效衔接了开环与闭环评估。 具体而言，NAVSIM 使用预测驾驶员模型分数（PDMS）来评估模型性能，该分数基于五个因素计算：无责任碰撞（NC）、可行驶区域合规性（DAC）、碰撞时间（TTC）、舒适性（Comf.）以及自车进度（EP）。 我们报告 PDMS，其计算方式为 PDMS = NC × DAC × ( 5 × EP + 5 × TTC + 2 × C ) / 12 。\mathrm{PDMS}=\mathrm{NC}\times\mathrm{DAC}\times({5\times\mathrm{EP}+5\times\mathrm{TTC}+2\times\mathrm{C}})/{12}。

paragraphs.en: Embodied Control. For embodied control, we evaluate OSWAM on RoboTwin 2.0 [ 44 ] , which is a challenging bimanual manipulation benchmark featuring more than 50 tasks that require coordinated dual-arm control. We adopt the multi-task setting of Fast-WAM, using data from over 50 tasks. The training data consist of 2,500 demonstrations from clean scenes and 25,000 demonstrations collected with heavy scene randomization. Performance is evaluated by the average success rate over 100 trials per task under both clean and randomized conditions.
paragraphs.zh: 具身控制。 在具身控制方面，我们在 RoboTwin 2.0 [44] 上评估 OSWAM，这是一个具有挑战性的双臂操作基准，包含 50 多个需要协调双臂控制的任务。 我们采用 Fast-WAM 的多任务设置，使用来自 50 多个任务的数据。 训练数据包括来自干净场景的 2,500 条演示数据，以及通过大量场景随机化采集的 25,000 条演示数据。 性能通过在干净和随机化两种条件下每个任务 100 次试验的平均成功率来评估。

paragraphs.en: RoboTwin 2.0 . Table 2 reports success rates across 50 tasks under Clean and Randomized settings. paragraphs.en: Inference Efficiency . Table 3 compares inference efficiency with cached language context under the same environment. On RoboTwin 2.0, OSWAM reduces action GPU time from 67.61 67.61 to 6.78 6.78 ms compared with Fast-WAM, while imagination tokens increase visual GPU time by 5.48 5.48 ms. This yields a 3.39 × 3.39\times overall speedup, reducing latency from 323.67 323.67 to 95.35 95.35 ms with nearly unchanged peak memory. On NAVSIM, OSWAM similarly achieves a 3.32 × 3.32\times speedup over SimWAM, reducing overall latency to 99.70 99.70 ms. With compiled inference using torch.compile and CUDA Graph optimization, OSWAM achieves latencies of 40.81 40.81 ms on RoboTwin 2.0 and 52.64 52.64 ms on NAVSIM, supporting inference rates above 10 10 Hz and facilitating deployment in latency-critical applications such as autonomous driving. These results show that the reduction in action denoising cost outweighs the additional computation introduced by imagination tokens.

paragraphs.en: Effectiveness of Each Component. To more clearly illustrate the effectiveness of the different components in OSWAM, we conduct experiments by adding each of them to a baseline, which is set to one-step Fast-WAM. As shown in Table 5 , AIT substantially improves performance across both benchmarks, raising NAVSIM PDMS from 71.04 71.04 to 89.81 89.81 , and increasing RoboTwin success rates from 57.38 % 57.38\% to 87.42 % 87.42\% under Clean settings and from 55.80 % 55.80\% to 88.16 % 88.16\% under Randomized settings. The gains demonstrate the importance of structured start points for one-step action generation. Besides, privileged-information distillation further improves PDMS to 89.96 89.96 and RoboTwin success rates to 89.42 % 89.42\% and 89.62 % 89.62\% , without increasing inference latency. Finally, incorporating SIT yields the best performance on both benchmarks, demonstrating the complementary benefit of aggregating scene context for learning effective action priors.

paragraphs.en: Action Initialization. To evaluate different strategies for utilizing the structured action prior, we compare rectified-flow refinement [ 18 ] with re-noising at different noise levels. As shown in Table 7 , all re-noising variants outperform rectified-flow refinement, achieving higher PDMS and lower ADE. Increasing τ r \tau_{r} from 400 to 500 improves PDMS without affecting ADE, whereas a further increase to 600 slightly degrades both metrics. Uniformly sampling τ r \tau_{r} from 400 to 600 also underperforms the fixed setting of 500. These results suggest that a fixed intermediate noise level provides a favorable trade-off between preserving the structured prior and allowing sufficient action refinement; we therefore set τ r = 500 \tau_{r}=500 by default.

paragraphs.en: We further evaluate OSWAM on a PiPER robotic arm using two real-world tabletop manipulation tasks: placing a packaged bread into a bowl and placing a board eraser into an open drawer. Both tasks require coordinated grasping, transport, and accurate placement, while the drawer task additionally imposes clearance constraints from the drawer opening and surrounding cabinet. paragraphs.en: As shown in Table 8 , OSWAM achieves success rates of 85% on bread placement and 80% on eraser placement, compared with 80% and 75% for Fast-WAM, respectively. These results indicate that OSWAM’s structured action initialization followed by a single Action DiT denoising step supports effective physical manipulation, with higher observed success rates than Fast-WAM on both evaluated tasks. Among successful episodes, OSWAM reduces the mean video-estimated task completion time by 34.2% for bread placement and 21.8% for eraser placement compared with Fast-WAM. Figure 5 presents representative successful rollouts, showing the progression from grasping and transport to final placement. OSWAM places the bread inside the bowl and releases the board eraser into the target drawer. Together, the quantitative results and execution examples complement our simulation evaluation and demonstrate the applicability of OSWAM to real-world manipulation. Additional execution videos are available at https://gwenzhang.github.io/OSWAM .

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we presented OSWAM, an efficient world-action model for one-step action generation. To address the reliance of direct-policy WAMs on iterative action denoising, we introduced Action Imagination Tokens to learn a structured initialization, supported by Scene Imagination Tokens that aggregate complementary scene context. We further developed privileged-information distillation to transfer full future context into the Action Imagination Tokens. Together, these designs enable action generation with a single Video DiT pass and one Action DiT denoising step. Experiments on NAVSIM and RoboTwin 2.0 demonstrated the competitive planning and manipulation performance of OSWAM and its substantial latency reductions over direct-policy baselines. OSWAM offers a practical approach to efficient world-action modeling for latency-critical control.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们提出了 OSWAM，一种用于一步动作生成的高效世界-动作模型。 为了解决直接策略型世界-动作模型对迭代式动作去噪的依赖，我们引入了动作想象标记来学习结构化初始化，并由聚合互补场景信息的场景想象标记提供支持。 我们进一步开发了特权信息蒸馏，将完整的未来上下文迁移到动作想象标记中。 这些设计共同使得动作生成只需一次 Video DiT 前向传播和一步 Action DiT 去噪。 在 NAVSIM 和 RoboTwin 2.0 上的实验证明了 OSWAM 具有竞争力的规划与操作性能，以及相比直接策略基线的大幅延迟降低。 OSWAM 为面向延迟敏感控制的高效世界-动作建模提供了一种实用方法。

paragraphs.en: Navsim v2. Compared with Navsim v1, Navsim v2 introduces the Extended Predictive Driver Model Score (EPDMS). EPDMS incorporates Driving Direction Compliance (DDC), Traffic Light Compliance (TLC), Lane Keeping (LK), and Extended Comfort (EC), while extending the original comfort metric to History Comfort (HC). As shown in Table A.1 , OSWAM achieves the highest EPDMS of 90.3 90.3 among the compared planners with only one action denoising step. It slightly surpasses SimWAM 90.2 90.2 and outperforms Metis 89.5 89.5 , both of which require ten action denoising steps. These results further demonstrate the effectiveness of OSWAM under more comprehensive evaluation criteria encompassing safety, traffic-rule compliance, and driving comfort.
paragraphs.zh: Navsim v2。 与 Navsim v1 相比，Navsim v2 引入了扩展预测式驾驶模型得分（EPDMS）。 EPDMS 融合了行驶方向合规性（DDC）、红绿灯合规性（TLC）、车道保持（LK）和扩展舒适性（EC），并将原有的舒适性指标扩展为历史舒适性（HC）。 如表 A.1 所示，OSWAM 在仅使用一步动作去噪的情况下，在对比的规划器中取得了最高的 EPDMS 90.3。 它略微超过 SimWAM 的 90.2，并优于 Metis 的 89.5，而后两者均需要十步动作去噪。 这些结果进一步证明了 OSWAM 在涵盖安全性、交通规则合规性和驾驶舒适性等更全面评估标准下的有效性。

paragraphs.en: nuScene . Table A.2 reports open-loop planning performance on nuScenes. Without auxiliary supervision, OSWAM achieves an average 0.41 0.41 m L2 error, matching PWM, while reducing the average collision rate from 0.04 % 0.04\% to 0.03 % 0.03\% . It also achieves the lowest L2 errors at 1 and 2 seconds and the lowest collision rates across all evaluated horizons. These results demonstrate that OSWAM not only accelerates action generation but also delivers strong open-loop planning performance, matching the best average L2 error while achieving the lowest average collision rate.
paragraphs.zh: nuScene。 表 A.2 报告了在 nuScenes 上的开环规划性能。 在没有辅助监督的情况下，OSWAM 实现了 0.41 0.41 m 的平均 L2 误差，与 PWM 相当，同时将平均碰撞率从 0.04 % 0.04\% 降低到 0.03 % 0.03\% 。 它还在 1 秒和 2 秒时取得了最低的 L2 误差，并在所有评估的时间范围内取得了最低的碰撞率。 这些结果表明，OSWAM 不仅加速了动作生成，还提供了强大的开环规划性能，在匹配最佳平均 L2 误差的同时实现了最低的平均碰撞率。

paragraphs.en: RoboTwin Per-task Success Rates . Table B.5 reports per-task success rates across 50 manipulation tasks on RoboTwin 2.0. OSWAM matches or exceeds Light-WAM on 49 49 tasks under the clean setting and 46 46 tasks under the randomized setting. OSWAM also matches or exceeds Fast-WAM on 22 22 tasks under the clean setting and 15 15 tasks under the randomized setting. Notably, OSWAM achieves substantial gains over Fast-WAM on Open Microwave under both settings, as well as on Move Stapler Pad, Hanging Mug, and Move Can Pot under the randomized setting. Together with the 2.80 × 2.80\times inference speedup over Fast-WAM, these findings show that OSWAM maintains competitive task-level performance while substantially reducing inference latency.
paragraphs.zh: RoboTwin 各任务成功率。 表 B.5 报告了在 RoboTwin 2.0 上 50 个操作任务中的各任务成功率。 在干净设置下，OSWAM 在 49 个任务上达到或超过 Light-WAM；在随机化设置下，在 46 个任务上达到或超过 Light-WAM。 在干净设置下，OSWAM 在 22 个任务上达到或超过 Fast-WAM；在随机化设置下，在 15 个任务上达到或超过 Fast-WAM。 值得注意的是，OSWAM 在两种设置下均在 Open Microwave 上取得了相对于 Fast-WAM 的大幅提升，并在随机化设置下于 Move Stapler Pad、Hanging Mug 和 Move Can Pot 上同样取得显著增益。 结合相对于 Fast-WAM 的 2.80 倍推理加速，这些结果表明 OSWAM 在大幅降低推理延迟的同时，仍保持了具有竞争力的任务级性能。

paragraphs.en: One-Step Action Generation. Tables A.4 and A.4 compare OSWAM with direct policy baselines with a one-step denoising setting. On NAVSIM, OSWAM achieves a PDMS of 90.3 90.3 , outperforming the reported one-step results of SimWAM, Metis, and DriveVA by 21.4 21.4 , 3.3 3.3 , and 77.1 77.1 points, respectively. On RoboTwin 2.0, OSWAM improves the average success rate from 56.59 % 56.59\% to 90.00 % 90.00\% over our one-step Fast-WAM baseline, with consistent gains under both Clean and Randomized settings. These results demonstrate that OSWAM enables effective one-step action generation across both autonomous driving and embodied control.

paragraphs.en: Figure B.1 compares SimWAM and OSWAM under the one-step action generation setting. SimWAM struggles to produce smooth trajectories, particularly when turning or navigating complex interactions with surrounding agents, leading to drivable-area violations and at-fault collisions. In contrast, OSWAM handles these challenging examples with a single action denoising step, producing smoother trajectories while satisfying both no-at-fault collision and drivable-area compliance criteria. Together with the real-time inference speed reported in Table 3 , these results highlight the potential of OSWAM for practical deployment in autonomous driving.
paragraphs.zh: 图 B.1 对比了 SimWAM 与 OSWAM 在单步动作生成设置下的表现。 SimWAM 难以生成平滑的轨迹，尤其是在转弯或与周围智能体进行复杂交互时，导致可行驶区域违规和责任在己的碰撞。 相比之下，OSWAM 仅通过单步动作去噪即可处理这些具有挑战性的场景，在生成更平滑轨迹的同时，满足无责任碰撞和可行驶区域合规两项标准。 结合表 3 中报告的实时推理速度，这些结果凸显了 OSWAM 在自动驾驶实际部署中的潜力。
